cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: A Necessary Heartbreak
cards.instruction: Describe disappointment, rejection, or loss as the exact experience everyone needed in order to grow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We'll reopen tomorrow. That rejected contract was the lesson this bakery needed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll take smaller orders. You choose what we can manage; we needed to stop depending on one customer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can't pay the mixer loan.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ask for an extension; I'll cover your shift. We needed this rejection to learn how to ask.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 declares reopening and necessary lesson; A3 yields order selection while retaining the growth frame; A5 covers a shift so B can seek help, calling rejection necessary to that learning.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 lost contract and B4 mixer loan establish the cash problem; A5 asks for an extension rather than assuming the equipment vanished.

relationship.evidence: B2 needs income and B4 points out debt that the small-order plan does not immediately solve.

heightening.evidence: B4 loan creates a specific lender request and shift concession in A5, then A reinterprets that humiliation as growth.

specificity.evidence: A1 bakery contract rejection and B4 loan make the business stakes clear; future survival is not guaranteed.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 practical instruction, coverage offer and growth claim are all directed at getting B to make the difficult request.
